metadata.executor_model: opus (fresh-context general-purpose subagent), the session default
metadata.release_gate_for: P42 v0.54.0 — the telemetry duty is ungated in work
metadata.baseline_note: without_skill baseline intentionally skipped: this is regression detection for a one-clause behavior change, not a skill-value study. Eval 2 not run — the change is orthogonal to the bugfix path, and the suite is a manual, costly gate.

notes: Release gate for P42, which removed the `Inside a /flywheel:loop cycle` precondition from work's telemetry duty. The decisive observation is not the grader's 7/7 but what the run produced alongside it: the executor, invoked STANDALONE with no /flywheel:loop anywhere, wrote four transition lines to .claude/flywheel/runs/apply-discount/2026-09-15.jsonl. That is the behavior P29 recorded as absent on 2026-09-09, when all six executors in that gate independently reported writing no telemetry.

Per-field omission held under real conditions rather than only in the unit tests: `commit` is omitted on every line because the eval workdir is not a git repo; `bytes_out` appears only on the lines that wrote files; `elapsed_s` is omitted on the `started` line, whose true start predates the executor's first timestamp; `bytes_in` appears only where it was actually measured. No line carries a tokens field, and none was zeroed to look complete.
No leak: `git status` on the plugin repo was clean after the run — the ungated write landed in the workdir, never in flywheel's own tree. check-fixture-leaks.sh stayed green.

Process deviation, recorded not hidden: the version was bumped to 0.54.0 BEFORE this gate ran, which inverts the CLAUDE.md rule that a work behavior change runs its eval before the bump. The gate passed, so the release stands, but the order was wrong.
